b1_name_version: legal-en-de-v2.1 · external name: arbitr Legal German
b1_status: Beta since 1 Sep 2026; GA planned 3 Nov 2026
b1_base_model: Fine-tuned from our general EN→DE engine v4 (in-house, proprietary licence)
b1_one_line: Cuts legal post-editing time for DACH legal and compliance teams
b2_use_cases:
1. Contracts and terms of service
2. Privacy notices and consent text
3. Regulatory filings and policy documents
b2_customers: In-house legal, compliance and procurement teams at EU enterprises; law-firm knowledge teams
b2_out_of_scope: Court filings and anything published without human legal review; Swiss and Austrian legal variants (use generic engine)
b2_oversight: Assurance level 2 minimum: every segment reviewed by a qualified legal linguist before publishing
b3_sources: 1.8M segments: 1.2M licensed EU legal corpus, 450k public EUR-Lex, 150k synthetic back-translation
b3_domains: Contracts, privacy and regulatory text. Thin on litigation and on Swiss/Austrian terminology
b3_cleaning: Near-duplicate removal, PII masking with regex + NER, length-ratio and QE-score filters
b3_customer_data: No customer data in the shared model
b4_metrics: arbitr Legal DE test v3 (2,000 segments, contracts + privacy)
arbitr Legal DE test v3 (2,000 segments)
b4_headline: Saves legal linguists about 22 minutes per 1,000 words (53 → 31) in a 40k-word pilot
b5_weaknesses: Very long sentences (60+ words), Swiss legal terms, nested defined terms
b5_errors: Defined-term inconsistency ("Agreement" rendered two ways); modal verb strength (shall/must) softened
b5_safety: Rare omissions of short negations in long clauses; no known prompt-injection exposure (not an LLM)
b5_mitigations: Terminology agent enforces defined terms; negation check flags missing 'nicht/kein'; mandatory human review
b6_limits: 512 tokens per segment; documents split at sentence boundaries
b6_formats: DOCX, XLIFF 1.2/2.0, JSON, HTML, plain text
b7_where: Machine translation step of the Legal workflow; before APE post-editing
b7_cortex: Reads approved legal glossary and TM from Cortex; does not write to it
b7_routing: Chosen automatically when content is tagged legal and the pair is EN→DE
b7_api: Available via arbitr API and the Drupal and Zendesk connectors
b8_versions: Retrained on licensed legal corpus; Beta release
c1_terminology: Glossary and do-not-translate lists enforced by the terminology agent; 98.6% enforcement on test set
c1_tm: 100% and fuzzy TM matches from Cortex are reused before MT; +6 pts leverage on legal content
c1_tags: XLIFF inline tags preserved; tag error rate 0.3% on test set
c1_post_edit: Pilot with 3 legal linguists: 22 min saved per 1,000 words (n=40k words)
c1_migration: Drop-in replacement for ModernMT legal profiles before the Dec 2026 sunset; TM migrates via Cortex import
c4_data_needed: Minimum 50k approved segments + glossary; ideal 250k segments and a style guide
c4_onboarding: 1. Customer shares TM and glossary  2. We clean and split data  3. Train and evaluate  4. Customer pilot  5. Go live
c4_uplift: +3 to +5 COMET on the customer's own held-out content in two pilots
c4_retraining: Quarterly, or after 20k new approved segments
c4_isolation: Dedicated weights and storage per customer; never pooled with other customers
c4_ownership: Customer owns fine-tuned weights; exported or deleted within 30 days of contract end
d1_how_sold: Add-on to Pro and Enterprise plans; customer-trained version is a one-off build fee
d1_pricing: Intelligence Credits per 1,000 words; build fee per customer model
d2_signals: Over 1M legal words a year into German; currently on ModernMT or DeepL; regulated industry
d2_disqualifiers: Needs Swiss/Austrian legal German; under 200k words a year; wants no human review
d2_questions: How many legal words do you translate into German a year? Who reviews them today? Which engine are you on, and when does it renew?
d2_objections: "DeepL is good enough" → show COMET and minutes-saved results on their own sample
d3_eval_offer: Free 2-week bake-off on up to 50k words of the customer's own legal content
d3_success: At least 15 minutes saved per 1,000 words, with no increase in critical errors
d3_request: Rep requests in the Model Factory; model team replies within 2 working days
d3_onboarding: 1. Signature  2. Connector set-up  3. Glossary import  4. First job  5. Review of first 10k words
d3_deliverables: Model card, evaluation report on their content, quality dashboard
d3_reporting: Monthly quality report: COMET trend, post-edit time, terminology enforcement
e_claims: Cuts post-editing time by about 40% vs our generic engine on legal EN→DE
B4 row 3 + C1 Post-edit effort: pilot, 3 legal linguists, 40k words, 19 Sep 2026
